questions.q: Dana can open the Incident and edit most fields, but not Assignment group. Why does this immediately point at a field-level ACL rather than a table-level one?
options: If the table-level write ACL were failing, she couldn't edit any field at all; the symptom is isolated to one field
There's no way to tell without opening the Security Debugger first
Field-level ACLs are always checked before table-level ACLs
Table-level ACLs never apply to the write operation
questions.explain: Table-level access is a prerequisite for any field access — since Dana can edit most fields, incident.write is clearly passing, and the problem narrows to the one blocked field.

questions.q: What does the Security Debugger trace show when reproducing Dana's issue?
options: That incident.write fails outright
That incident.write passes and incident.assignment_group fails
That no ACLs apply to this record at all
That Dana's user record is disabled
questions.explain: The debugger names incident.write as passing (role: itil) and incident.assignment_group as the specific failing field-level ACL.

questions.q: What ingredient of incident.assignment_group is actually responsible for blocking Dana's edit?
options: A condition comparing the Priority field
A script checking whether the current user is a member of the group in current.assignment_group
A Requires role entry that excludes itil
There is no ACL on this field at all; it's a UI policy
questions.explain: The field-level ACL has no role requirement and no condition — only a script that checks group membership against the record's current assignment group.

questions.q: Why did the same ACL pass for Dana last month but fail this month, even though her role never changed?
options: This month's incident is assigned to a group Dana isn't a member of, so the script's group-membership check now returns answer = false
The Security Debugger was turned off last month
The ACL was deleted and recreated
Dana's itil role was temporarily revoked
questions.explain: The script's result depends on which group the record is currently assigned to relative to Dana's group memberships, not on her role — that's why the outcome changed without any role change.

questions.q: If the business requirement is actually "only the current assignment group can reassign incidents," what should the admin do about Dana's ticket?
options: Elevate to security_admin and rewrite the script immediately
Delete the field-level ACL entirely
Explain the real behavior to Dana and have her request reassignment through her team lead or the assigned group, since the ACL is working as intended
Add the itil role to the ACL's Requires role list
questions.explain: When the ACL's behavior matches the actual business rule, no fix is needed — only elevate and edit the ACL script if the underlying requirement has genuinely changed.
